unit.title: Decimals
unit.blurb: Ordering decimals, adding and subtracting decimals, multiplying and dividing decimals by whole numbers, and mental strategies.

lesson.t: Why we line up the points
p: Lining up the decimal points lines up the place values: ones under ones, tenths under tenths. You can only add tenths to tenths, just as you add tens to tens.
Filling with zeros (2.6 = 2.60) does not change the value; it keeps the columns tidy.
Check by adding back: 3.65 + 2.35 = 6.00.

p: Divide a decimal by a whole number with short division. Keep the decimal point in line: 7.2 ÷ 3 = 2.4.
Add zeros if you need more places: 3.4 ÷ 4 = 3.40 ÷ 4 = 0.85.

lesson.t: Why the point stays in line
p: 7.2 ÷ 3: 7 ones ÷ 3 = 2 ones, remainder 1 one = 10 tenths. 10 + 2 = 12 tenths ÷ 3 = 4 tenths. So 7.2 ÷ 3 = 2.4.
Each digit of the answer has the same place value as the digit above it, so the point lines up.
